title: Theorem A
body_md:
The divisor $27379H-8658E$ is nef on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ at ten very general points.
Equivalently, every plane curve of degree $d$ with multiplicities $m_i$ at these points satisfies
$$
27379\,d\ge8658\sum_{i=1}^{10}m_i.
$$
In particular,
$$
\varepsilon_{10}\ge\frac{8658}{27379}=0.3162277658059\ldots.
$$
head: environment

title: Theorem B
body_md:
Suppose a ten-point blow-up over $\mathbb{F}_p$ carries a unique divisor $\Gamma_0\in\lvert \Theta\rvert$, and write $\Gamma_0=\tilde A+\tilde B$.
Assume that $\tilde A$ and $\tilde B$ are smooth geometrically irreducible strict transforms of plane curves, meeting transversally at $k\ge1$ points.
Let their classes be $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and suppose that
$$
h^0(\alpha)=h^0(\beta)=1,\qquad
\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{ob}_\Theta=10,\qquad
\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{ob}_\alpha,\operatorname{ob}_\beta)=10+k.
$$
Then a complex ten-point blow-up carries a smooth irreducible curve $\Gamma\in\lvert \Theta\rvert$ with $\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{ob}_\Theta=10$.
Such configurations occur in a family of dimension $10$ in the space of ordered configurations.
head: environment
name: Lifting and smoothing criterion

label: prop:refl
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:refl}
Let $\Gamma\subset X_0$ be a smooth connected curve of class $\gamma$ such that the bundle $N_{\Gamma/\mathcal{X}}$ is semistable of slope $-\kappa<0$, so that $\gamma^2=-2\kappa$. If $D$ is nef on $X_0$, then
$$
s_\gamma(D)=D+\frac{D\cdot\gamma}{\kappa}\,\gamma
$$
is nef on $X_t$ for all but countably many $t\in T$, and hence on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at ten very general points.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $c$ be the class of an effective divisor on the geometric generic fibre of $\mathcal{X}\to T$. This divisor is defined over a finite extension of $\mathbb{C}(T)$. Taking the sum of its Galois conjugates, we obtain a divisor defined over $\mathbb{C}(T)$ whose closure $\mathcal{C}\subset\mathcal{X}$ is flat over $T$ and has generic class $ec$ for some integer $e\ge1$. Let us stress that we do not perform any base change here, since a ramified base change would kill the Kodaira--Spencer class and split \eqref{eq:N}.

Denote by $\mu$ the multiplicity of $\mathcal{C}$ along $\Gamma$. A local equation of $\mathcal{C}$ defines a non-zero map $\mathcal{O}_\Gamma(-\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sym}^\mu N^\vee_{\Gamma/\mathcal{X}}$. Since we are in characteristic zero, the target is semistable of slope $\mu\kappa$, and hence $-e\,c\cdot\gamma\le\mu\kappa$. This shows that
$$
s_\gamma(ec)=\bigl(\mathcal{C}|_{X_0}-\mu\Gamma\bigr)+\Bigl(\mu+\frac{ec\cdot\gamma}{\kappa}\Bigr)\Gamma
$$
is effective on $X_0$. As $s_\gamma$ is a self-adjoint isometry, we get $e\,s_\gamma(D)\cdot c=D\cdot s_\gamma(ec)\ge0$. So $s_\gamma(D)$ is nef on the geometric generic fibre.

Now let $c$ be a class with $s_\gamma(D)\cdot c<0$. The relative Hilbert scheme of curves of class $c$ is proper over $T$ and does not dominate $T$, so it lies over finitely many points of $T$. Since there are only countably many such classes, $s_\gamma(D)$ is nef on $X_t$ for all but countably many $t$.

Finally, for each such class $c$, the configurations on which $c$ is effective form a closed subset of the configuration space. This subset misses the general point of $T$, so it is proper. Therefore $s_\gamma(D)$ is nef at a very general configuration.
head: environment

label: prop:ss
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For (a), since $H^1(\mathcal{O}_{X_0})=H^2(\mathcal{O}_{X_0})=0$, the sequence $0\to\mathcal{O}_{X_0}\to\mathcal{O}_{X_0}(\Gamma)\to N_{\Gamma/X_0}\to0$ gives $H^1(N_{\Gamma/X_0})\cong H^1(\mathcal{O}_{X_0}(\Gamma))$. The vanishing of $H^1(\mathbb{P}^2,\mathcal{O}(d))$ identifies this group with $\operatorname{coker} M$. A first-order lift is a polynomial $f_1$ with $M(Z_0)f_1=-(\partial_vM)f$, see \cite[\S3.2]{Ser}.

For (b), observe that a saturated line subbundle of $N_{\Gamma/\mathcal{X}}$ other than $N_{\Gamma/X_0}$ maps non-trivially to $\mathcal{O}_\Gamma$, so it has degree at most $0$. Since $\deg N_{\Gamma/\mathcal{X}}=-1$, such a subbundle destabilizes if and only if it is $\mathcal{O}_\Gamma$, that is, if and only if \eqref{eq:N} splits.
head: environment

label: cor:red
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:red}
Suppose that some complex ten-point blow-up $X_Z$ carries a smooth irreducible curve $\Gamma\in\lvert \Theta\rvert$ with $\operatorname{ob}\ne0$. Then $27379H-8658E$ is nef on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at ten very general points.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let us move the points along a line in a direction $v$ with $\operatorname{ob}(v)\ne0$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:ss}(b), the bundle $N_{\Gamma/\mathcal{X}}$ is semistable of slope $-\tfrac12$. Now Proposition~\ref{prop:refl} applied with $D=H$ and $\kappa=\tfrac12$ gives the nefness of $s_\Theta(H)=27379H-8658E$.
head: environment

label: thm:seed
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:seed}
Let $Z_0\in\operatorname{Conf}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ be a configuration, with blow-up $X_0$, satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)}]
\item We have $h^0(X_0,\Theta)=1$, and $\operatorname{ob}_\Theta$ has rank $h^1(X_0,\Theta)=10$.
\item The member of $\lvert \Theta\rvert$ is $\Gamma_0=\tilde A+\tilde B$. Here $A$ and $B$ are absolutely irreducible plane curves whose strict transforms $\tilde A,\tilde B$ are smooth and meet transversally at $k\ge1$ points $n_1,\dots,n_k$. Neither of them contains an exceptional curve.
\item For the classes $\alpha,\beta$ of $\tilde A,\tilde B$ we have $h^0(\alpha)=h^0(\beta)=1$, and the combined map $v\mapsto(\operatorname{ob}_\alpha v,\operatorname{ob}_\beta v)$ has rank $h^1(\alpha)+h^1(\beta)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist ten distinct points $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ such that $X_Z$ carries a smooth irreducible curve $\Gamma\in\lvert \Theta\rvert$ with $\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{ob}_{\Theta}=10$. Moreover, such configurations occur in a family of dimension $10$ in the space of ordered configurations, before quotienting by projective transformations.
head: environment
name: Arithmetic lifting and smoothing

label: lem:smooth
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:smooth}
Let $c_1,\dots,c_s$ be interpolation classes with $h^0(X_0,c_i)=1$ and $h^1(X_0,c_i)=r_i$, and suppose that the combined obstruction map has rank $r=\sum_ir_i$. Then, near $Z_0$, the scheme $\bigcap_iL_{c_i}$ is smooth over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of relative dimension $20-r$. Moreover, at each of its points we have $h^0(c_i)=1$, and $\operatorname{ob}_{c_i}$ has rank $r_i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the local ring of $\operatorname{Conf}$ at $Z_0$, and write $M=M_{c_i}$ in block form with $M_{11}$ invertible over $\mathcal{O}$ of size $\operatorname{rank}M(Z_0)$. Row and column operations bring $M$ to the form $\operatorname{diag}(1,S)$, where
$$
S=M_{22}-M_{21}M_{11}^{-1}M_{12}
$$
is the Schur complement, a column of length $r_i$. The maximal minors of $M$ generate the ideal of the entries of $S$. Put $f=(-M_{11}^{-1}M_{12},1)^t$ and $W=(-M_{21}M_{11}^{-1},1)$, so that $S=WMf$. At $Z_0$ we have $Mf=0$ and $WM=0$, hence $d_vS=W(\partial_vM)f=\operatorname{ob}_{c_i}(v)$ in the basis $W$ of the left kernel. Therefore the $r$ Schur entries have linearly independent relative differentials modulo $p$. Together with $p$ they form a part of a regular system of parameters, and the claim follows from the Jacobian criterion.
head: environment

label: lem:spec
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:spec}
Let $D$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field finite over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $Z\colon\operatorname{Spec}D\to L_\Theta$ be a morphism sending the closed point to $Z_0$. If the geometric generic member of the corresponding family is reducible, then the generic point of $Z$ lies in $L_\alpha\cap L_\beta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f_Z$ be a primitive equation over $D$. Its reduction spans $\ker M_\Theta(Z_0)$, so it is a unit times $AB$. After a finite extension of $D$ we can write $f_Z=gh$ with $g,h$ primitive and non-constant, by Gauss's lemma. The reductions $\bar g,\bar h$ are homogeneous of the same degrees as $g,h$. Since $A$ and $B$ are absolutely irreducible and not associated, we get $\{\bar g,\bar h\}=\{A,B\}$ up to units, say $\bar g=A$.

Moreover, Hasse derivatives reduce to Hasse derivatives, so $\operatorname{mult}_zg\le\operatorname{mult}_{\bar z}\bar g$ at every point. Combined with the inequality $\operatorname{mult}_zg+\operatorname{mult}_zh\ge37=\operatorname{mult}_{\bar z}A+\operatorname{mult}_{\bar z}B$, this shows that all these inequalities are equalities. Hence $g$ has class $\alpha$ and $h$ has class $\beta$, which completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:nodes
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nodes}
Formally at $n_j$, the family $\mathcal{C}$ is given by $\xi\eta=\tau_j$ with $\tau_j\in\mathfrak{m}_R$. Moreover, $\tau_j\notin pR$ for every $j$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
After an unramified extension of $\mathbb{Z}_p$, which does not affect the argument, the nodes and their branches are rational. The first assertion is then the versal deformation of a split node.

Suppose now that $\tau_1\in pR$. In $\bar R=R/p\cong\mathbb{F}_p[[u]]$, the locus $V(\bar\tau_2,\dots,\bar\tau_k)$ has dimension at least $10-(k-1)$. This is bigger than $\dim(L_\alpha\cap L_\beta)_{\mathbb{F}_p}=10-k$, so there is a curve germ in this locus which is not contained in $L_\alpha\cap L_\beta$. Let $D$ be its normalization. Over $D$ all the nodes persist, so near each $n_j$ the family is $D[[\xi,\eta]]/(\xi\eta)$, and away from the nodes it is smooth over $D$.

Normalizing along the node sections, we obtain a proper smooth family over $D$ with special fibre $\tilde A\sqcup\tilde B$. In such a family the number of geometric connected components is locally constant, since the Stein factorization is finite \'etale. Hence the generic member is reducible, and Lemma~\ref{lem:spec} shows that the germ lies in $L_\alpha\cap L_\beta$, a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If an unramified extension was used to split the nodes, we make that extension throughout the following argument, replacing $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by its ring of integers; we retain the same notation.
Choose a non-zero element $a\in\mathfrak{a}$. Since $R$ is a domain, $F=a\prod_j\tau_j$ is non-zero. A non-zero power series in $\mathbb{Z}_p[[u]]$ does not vanish identically on $(p\mathbb{Z}_p)^{10}$; this follows from Strassmann's theorem by induction on the number of variables. Hence there is $u^0\in(p\mathbb{Z}_p)^{10}$ with $F(u^0)\ne0$, which defines a point $Z\in L_\Theta(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ over $Z_0$.

Since $a(Z)\ne0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:spec} shows that $\Gamma_Z$ is geometrically irreducible. By properness, a singular point of $\Gamma_Z$ over $\mathbb{C}_p$ would specialize to one of the nodes $n_j$. But near $n_j$ the curve $\Gamma_Z$ is given by $\xi\eta=\tau_j(Z)\ne0$, so it is smooth there. Hence $\Gamma_Z$ is smooth. Furthermore, $\operatorname{ob}_\Theta$ has rank $10$ at $Z$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth}.

To pass to $\mathbb{C}$, consider the finite-type effectivity scheme defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the same interpolation minors.
On the open locus where the kernel is a line, it carries the corresponding universal divisor on the blown-up family.
Smoothness and geometric irreducibility of its fibres, together with the rank-$10$ condition on $\operatorname{ob}_\Theta$, define an open locus after shrinking around the point just constructed; see \cite[9.7.7]{EGA} for geometric irreducibility in families.
Our construction gives a point of this locus over a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ (allowing the unramified extension used to split the nodes).
It is therefore a nonempty finite-type scheme over $\mathbb{Q}$, and has a point over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, hence over $\mathbb{C}$.
The same Jacobian calculation as in Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth} makes this locus smooth of dimension $10$.
This proves the claimed dimension without requiring an embedding of a $p$-adic field into $\mathbb{C}$.
head: environment

label: thm:cert
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cert}
The configuration $Z_0$ satisfies conditions \textup{(S1)--(S3)} of Theorem~\ref{thm:seed} with $k=2$. More precisely, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $h^0(\Theta)=1$, $h^1(\Theta)=10$, and $\operatorname{ob}_\Theta$ has rank $10$. The unique member $f_0=AB$ is $g$-invariant.
\item The curve $A$ has degree $12$, multiplicity $5$ at $P$, multiplicity $4$ at the points of $\langle g\rangle q_1\cup\langle g\rangle q_2$, and multiplicity $3$ at the points of $\langle g\rangle q_3$; so $\alpha^2=-4$ and $\tilde A\cong\mathbb{P}^1$. The curve $B$ has degree $105$ and multiplicities $32$, $33$, $34$ at the same sets of points; so $\beta^2=-1$ and $\tilde B$ has genus $9$.
\item Both $A$ and $B$ are absolutely irreducible. At the ten points they have ordinary multiple points, and they have no other singular points, neither affine nor at infinity.
\item We have $i_P(A,B)=5\cdot32+2$, and $i_z(A,B)=\operatorname{mult}_zA\cdot\operatorname{mult}_zB$ at the remaining nine points; these numbers sum up to $12\cdot105$. The tangent cones of $A$ and $B$ at $P$ have greatest common divisor $xy$. Hence $\tilde A$ and $\tilde B$ meet transversally at two points of $E_P$, and $\alpha\cdot\beta=2$.
\item $h^0(\alpha)=h^0(\beta)=1$, $h^1(\alpha)=3$, $h^1(\beta)=9$, the obstruction maps have ranks $3$ and $9$, and together they have rank $12$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
All the properties listed above were computed twice, by two independent methods; the results are summarized in Table~\ref{tab:cert}.

In the first method we work with the interpolation matrices modulo $127$. These have size $7030\times7021$ for $\Theta$ and $5679\times5671$ for $\beta$. Their ranks were computed with our own elimination routine and with \textsc{FLINT} \cite{FLINT}; the factorization and the resultants were also computed with \textsc{FLINT}.

The second method does not use interpolation matrices at all, and it was carried out in \textsc{Singular} \cite{Sing}. Since the ideals $\mathfrak{m}_z^{m_z}$ are pairwise comaximal, the fat point ideal $I=\bigcap_z\mathfrak{m}_z^{m_z}$ is equal to the product $\prod_{j\ge1}I(S_j)$, where $S_j=\{z:m_z\ge j\}$ and $I(S_j)$ is the ideal of these points. We computed a standard basis of $I$ and checked that $\dim R/I=7030$. For a degree ordering, the image in $R/I$ of the polynomials of degree at most $d$ is spanned by the standard monomials of degree at most $d$. Therefore $h^0$ and $h^1$ are obtained by counting standard monomials, and the part of degree bigger than $d$ of a normal form realizes the projection $R/I\to\operatorname{coker} M$.

Moreover, since $\partial_xf\in\mathfrak{m}_z^{m_z-1}$, the obstruction of the motion $\partial/\partial x_z$ is represented by the part of degree bigger than $d$ of
$$
\operatorname{NF}\Bigl(\partial_xf\cdot\prod_{w\ne z}L_w^{m_w}\Bigr)\Big/\prod_{w\ne z}L_w(z)^{m_w},
$$
where $L_w$ is a line passing through $w$ and not through $z$. In order to check that $A$ and $B$ have no singular points outside $Z_0$, we compared the length of $R/(A,A_x,A_y)$ with the sum of the local lengths at the ten points. We obtained $81$ for $A$ and $8092$ for $B$ in both cases, and we checked the points at infinity after homogenizing. For the irreducibility check, one first verifies that $A$ and $B$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_{127}$.
Each also has a smooth $\mathbb{F}_{127}$-rational point outside $Z_0$.
These two facts together imply absolute irreducibility: Frobenius acts transitively on the geometric components of an irreducible curve, whereas the unique geometric component through a smooth rational point is Frobenius-stable.
A smooth rational point alone would not suffice without the first check.

As a consistency check, the eight infinitesimal projective motions lie in all three kernels. The stacked matrix $[\operatorname{ob}_\Theta;\operatorname{ob}_\alpha;\operatorname{ob}_\beta]$ has rank $12$, which means that $\ker\operatorname{ob}_\alpha\cap\ker\operatorname{ob}_\beta\subset\ker\operatorname{ob}_\Theta$.

label: cor:counterexample
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:counterexample}
A plane curve violating Nagata's inequality at ten very general points has degree at least $8658$ and total multiplicity at least $27379$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $S=\sum_i m_i$.
Theorem~A and the assumed violation give
$$
\sqrt{10}<\frac{S}{d}\le\frac{27379}{8658}.
$$
Since $4443/1405<\sqrt{10}$ and $1405\cdot27379-4443\cdot8658=1$, we obtain
$$
1\le1405S-4443d\le\frac{d}{8658}.
$$
Thus $d\ge8658$, and $S>\sqrt{10}\,d$ implies $S\ge27379$.
head: environment

label: rem:search
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:search}
Let us briefly explain how the configuration $Z_0$ was found. A $\mathbb{Z}/3$-invariant curve of class $\Theta$ lies in one of the three eigenspaces of forms of degree $117$ with multiplicity $37$ at the fixed point $P$; for the trivial character this space has dimension $2106$. The three free orbits impose $2109$ conditions, so the $\Theta$-locus is expected to have codimension $4$ in the $4$-parameter family of pairs $(q_2,q_3)$.

We tested all $2\,301\,061$ configurations of this type over $\mathbb{F}_{127}$, up to a symmetry group of order $108$, which took about $14$ core-hours. We found $3735$ configurations with a unique invariant member, and none of these members is irreducible. In fact, $3713$ of them have a multiple component, $21$ are reduced with three to five components, and only $Z_0$ gives a reduced member with exactly two components.

It is worth noticing that $Z_0$ is a transverse point of the symmetric family, since the corresponding $4\times4$ Jacobian determinant equals $59\ne0$. Moreover, the pair $(A,B)$ is rigid, because the tangent space to $L_\alpha\cap L_\beta$ consists only of the projective motions.
head: environment

label: prop:aut
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:aut}
If $\Gamma\in\lvert \Theta\rvert$ on $X_Z$ is preserved by an automorphism $\sigma$ of $X_Z$, then $\sigma$ is induced by a projective transformation permuting the points of $Z$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The pull-back $\sigma^*$ fixes $K$ and $\Theta$, hence it fixes $\Theta+37K=6H$, and so it fixes $H$. Therefore $\sigma$ commutes with the morphism $X_Z\to\mathbb{P}^2$ given by $\lvert H\rvert$.
head: environment

label: prop:inv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:inv}
If $Z$ is invariant under an involution of $\mathbb{P}^2$, then every member of $\lvert \Theta\rvert$ is reducible.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Every involution is conjugate to $\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1)$, with axis $x=0$ and centre $(1:0:0)$. The forms of degree $117$ which are even in $x$ span a space of dimension $3540$. A pair $\{q,\sigma q\}$ imposes at most $703$ conditions on these forms. A point on the axis imposes $361$ conditions, since only even jets matter. The centre imposes $342$ conditions, coming from the jets of odd degree.

If four of the points lie on the axis, then the axis is a component of every member, since $\Theta\cdot(H-E_1-\dots-E_4)<0$. Otherwise, a direct check of the possible orbit types shows that the points impose at most $3534$ conditions. Hence $h^0(\Theta)\ge6$. But a class of negative self-intersection with $h^0\ge2$ has a fixed component, so every member is reducible.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
We ran a census of the cyclic types with distinct weights, excluding homologies and types with four collinear points. It leaves two types for which the $\Theta$-locus has non-negative expected dimension and a count of semi-invariants does not already force $h^0(\Theta)\ge2$. These are $\mathbb{Z}/5$ with orbits $5+5$, where the expected codimension is $2$ in a $2$-parameter family, and $\mathbb{Z}/3$ with orbits $3+3+3+1$ from Section~\ref{sec:cert}.

In the $\mathbb{Z}/5$ family we scanned the sixteen primes $p\equiv1\pmod5$ with $131\le p\le491$, and every member of $\lvert \Theta\rvert$ we found is reducible. The most common splittings have components of degrees $95+11+11$ and $87+30$. The splitting $\theta_2+(57H-18E)$ also occurs, where $\theta_2=60H-19E$ is the class from Remark~\ref{rem:rung4}.

label: rem:rung4
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rung4}
Our approach also gives a short proof of Petrakiev's bound. Let $p=131$, let $\zeta$ be a primitive fifth root of unity, and consider
$$
Z=\langle\operatorname{diag}(\zeta,\zeta^{-1},1)\rangle\cdot\{(1:1:1),(49:14:1)\}.
$$
The blow-up $X_Z$ carries a smooth elliptic curve $T\in\lvert 60H-19E\rvert$ with $T^2=-10$ and $h^0=1$. This point is Hensel-liftable in the symmetric family, since the Jacobian determinant is $63$, so $T$ lifts to a smooth curve over $\mathbb{Z}_{131}$, and hence over $\mathbb{C}$. Moreover, $h^1(N_T)=10$ and the obstruction map has rank $10$, which persists on the lift.

The destabilizing extensions form a cone of dimension at most $9<10$ in $H^1(N_T)$. So for a general motion the bundle $N_{T/\mathcal{X}}$ is semistable, and Proposition~\ref{prop:refl} gives the nefness of $s_T(H)=H+12T=721H-228E$. In other words, the bound $d/m\ge2280/721$ follows from the existence of a single curve.
head: environment
name: Petrakiev's bound from a single elliptic curve
